text:
li: quick sync after the continuous-batcher RFC follow-up. two decisions: where admission ends and coalescer begins, and how to handle eviction/preempt for fairness. saw small-request p50 jump under tenant-heavy load.

arpita: can you share numbers?

li: p50 ~8-token requests went 10ms->30ms during tenant spike, p95 increased modestly. admission seems to be reserving bigger footprints than coalescer ultimately dispatches.

noah: we have three high-level options:
1) strict-reserve: admission predicts worst-case kernel tokens and locks that quota. simple accounting, but admission needs heavier estimation.
2) hint-reserve + reconcile: admission gives hints; coalescer emits deltas at dispatch and ledger reconciles. cheaper admission, more control-plane updates.
3) short-lease credits: admission hands short-lived leases with tokens; coalescer consumes; unused credit expires/reclaimed. aligns with time-bounded preemption windows.

arpita: trial of hint-reserve showed ledger hot-keys; devops-bot: control-plane ops +30% during test.

li: preemption: keep soft-trim as default, escalate to hard preempt only when queue depth > threshold or when retries exceed N. hybrid keeps KV stability but avoids starvation.

noah: API sketch: Reserve(tenant,hint)->{lease_id,reserved,ttl}; Dispatch(lease_id,used,attempt_id)->{delta}. attempt_id for idempotency. Ledger.delta should be batched per-cohort to avoid QPS spikes.

arpita: observability: per-lease trace, reserved vs actual, trim reason, affected tenants. Without this we can't debug tail cases.

li: rollout: land proto behind flag, run canary on staging-batcher, enable strict-mode for enterprise tenants first. owners: arpita (admission), noah (coalescer), li (proto+telemetry). devops-bot: canary scheduled Tue 06:00 UTC.

noah: agree on tiered contracts: strict for SLA customers, hint/pack for low-cost tiers. Also add circuit-breaker: if ledger latency high, fallback to conservative mode (no reconciliation) to protect control-plane.

li: thanks all. i'll open follow-up PR with proto + test plan.
